definitions.explanation: An alcoholic beverage brewed from rice, water, and koji mold. The term specifically distinguishes traditional Japanese alcohol from foreign alcoholic drinks.

examples.japanese: {日本酒|にほんしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一杯|いっぱい}→一杯：01793_ippai⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{日本酒|にほんしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{辛口|からくち}→辛口：18794_karakuchi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{飲|の}みやすい→飲みやすい：21767_nomiyasui⟧。
examples.english: This sake is dry and easy to drink.

examples.japanese: {日本酒|にほんしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{冷|ひ}や→冷や：28141_hiya⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{熱燗|あつかん}→熱燗：27548_atsukan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しめる→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{魅力|みりょく}→魅力：03749_miryoku⟧だ。
examples.english: The appeal of sake is that you can enjoy it chilled or hot.

notes:
USAGE:
{日本酒|にほんしゅ} specifically means sake brewed in the Japanese tradition, as distinct from ⟦{洋酒|ようしゅ}→洋酒：27829_youshu⟧ (Western liquor) or other foreign drinks. In casual speech, Japanese people often say simply ⟦お{酒|さけ}→お酒：01045_osake⟧ or ⟦{酒|さけ}→酒：02211_sake⟧, which can mean either sake specifically or alcohol in general depending on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日本酒|にほんしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧: to drink sake
- ⟦{辛口|からくち}→辛口：18794_karakuchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{日本酒|にほんしゅ}: dry sake
- ⟦{甘口|あまくち}→甘口：18197_amakuchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{日本酒|にほんしゅ}: sweet sake
- ⟦{熱燗|あつかん}→熱燗：27548_atsukan⟧: hot sake
- ⟦{冷|ひ}や→冷や：28141_hiya⟧ / ⟦{冷酒|れいしゅ}→冷酒：27547_reishu⟧: chilled sake

CULTURAL NOTE:
Sake brewing has a long history in Japan. Key terms include ⟦{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}→純米酒：25651_junmaishu⟧ (pure rice sake), ⟦{吟醸|ぎんじょう}→吟醸：25617_ginjou⟧ (premium sake), and ⟦{大吟醸|だいぎんじょう}→大吟醸：25652_daiginjou⟧ (super premium sake).
